title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Chrysostom Hom. 45 — mysteries spiritually; intelligible gift of body and blood
pass_a_gloss: The FORMER, about to remove Carnality from all Mysteries, and so from the Sacred Supper both the carnal presence and the participation of Christ’s body, comments thus in Homily 45 on John: Mysteries, he says, are not to be considered and contemplated carnally, but with interior eyes, i.e. spiritually; For such is the nature of Mysteries. And a few words interposed, he proceeds thus: As in Baptism, by the sensible element water, the intelligible gift of Regeneration; so also this INTELLIGIBLE gift of Christ’s body and blood is perceived not by any corporeal or sensible action, but by the spiritual intelligence of faith, with soul and mind.
pass_b_english: Chrysostom (Hom. 45 on John) strips carnality from the mysteries and from the Supper’s carnal presence and participation.

Mysteries are for interior eyes — spiritual. As baptism’s sensible water carries an intelligible regeneration-gift, so the intelligible gift of body and blood is received by faith’s spiritual intelligence, not by bodily action.
source_text: PRIOR uti à Mysteriis omnibus Carnalitatem, sic à S. Cœna, corporis Christi carnalem tùm præsentiam, tùm participationem, semoturus, Homil. 45. in Johannem ita commentatur: Mysteria, inquit, non sunt carnaliter, sed interioribus oculis, i. e. spiritualiter, consideranda & contemplanda; Hujusmodi enim est Mysteriorum natura. Et paucis interjectis, sic pergit: Sicut in Baptismo, sensibili aqua elemento, intelligibile Regenerationis donum; ita etiam INTELLIGIBILE hoc corporis & sanguinis Christi donum, non corporea aut sensibili aliquâ actione, sed spirituali fidei intelligentiâ, animo atque mente percipitur.
